title: She Scored 90 Off 62 Balls and Never Got Out. Campbelle Destroyed the Defending Champions.
excerpt: West Indies chased 163 in 19.5 overs as Shemaine Campbelle dismantled New Zealand at the Rose Bowl. Scotland won their first-ever World Cup match. And India face Pakistan at Edgbaston on Sunday.
body:
She came in at No. 3 with the chase barely underway. She left with 90 runs off 62 balls, an unbeaten performance that blew apart the defending champions and announced the West Indies as serious contenders in the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup.

Shemaine Campbelle's masterclass at the Rose Bowl in Southampton on Saturday was the highlight of Day 2 at the tournament in England — a day that saw three matches produce three decisive results and set the stage for Sunday's blockbuster: India versus Pakistan at Edgbaston.

## Campbelle Dismantles the Defending Champions

New Zealand, the reigning T20 World Cup holders after their 2024 triumph in Sharjah, batted first and posted 162/6 in their 20 overs. Brooke Halliday top-scored with 40 off 32 balls, while Aaliyah Alleyne was the pick of the West Indies bowlers with outstanding figures of 4/27 from her four overs.

It was a competitive total, but Campbelle — the 33-year-old Guyanese wicketkeeper-batter playing in her 155th T20I — made it look insufficient. She anchored the chase from the third over onwards, hitting boundaries with precision and rotating the strike with the composure of a veteran playing her final major tournament.

West Indies chased down the target in 19.5 overs, winning by seven wickets. Campbelle's 90 not out is now her career-best T20I score, and it earned her the Player of the Match award. Captain Hayley Matthews provided steady support, while Deandra Dottin's presence in the lineup added the firepower that keeps bowlers guessing even when she is not the one scoring.

## Scotland Make History at Old Trafford

Earlier in the day, Scotland recorded their first-ever victory in a T20 World Cup. Kathryn Bryce anchored the innings with 60 off 39 balls as Scotland posted 161/5 at Old Trafford in front of 7,543 fans.

Ireland, chasing, were bowled out for 121 in 19.1 overs, with Kirstie Gordon taking 3/16 to seal a comprehensive 40-run victory. For a nation that has spent years on the fringes of world cricket, it was a milestone — and a warning to bigger teams that the expanded format has brought genuine competition.

## Australia Assert Dominance Over South Africa

In the day's second match at Old Trafford, Australia reminded everyone why they entered the tournament as favourites. Batting first after winning the toss, Australia posted 172/8, with Phoebe Litchfield continuing her excellent form.

South Africa's chase fell apart, bowled out for 107 in 16.4 overs. The 65-run margin was emphatic, and it confirmed a pattern: Australia in World Cups are a different proposition from Australia in bilateral series. Sophie Molineux's squad is playing with the intensity of a team that lost semi-finals in 2024 and the 50-over World Cup in 2025, and is determined not to let a third trophy slip.

## India vs Pakistan: Sunday at Edgbaston

All of which leads to Sunday's main event. India face Pakistan at Edgbaston in Birmingham at 2 PM local time (6:30 PM IST), and Harmanpreet Kaur's side carries the weight of a nation's expectations.

India enters the tournament as reigning ODI World Cup champions, bolstered by three seasons of the Women's Premier League that have sharpened their squad's ability to perform under immense pressure. Pakistan, who qualified through the tournament qualifier, will look to their experienced top order — Sidra Ameen, Muneeba Ali, and Fatima Sana — to challenge India's bowling attack.

The head-to-head record in T20 World Cups heavily favours India, and Harmanpreet herself has six wins in eight World Cup encounters against Pakistan. But the biggest India-Pakistan cricket matches are rarely decided by history.

For millions of diaspora viewers — watching on Star Sports and JioHotstar in India, and on Willow TV or ICC.tv in the US and UK — the fixture needs no further selling. The start time of 6:30 PM IST makes this a prime-time evening watch across India and an early-morning event for NRIs on the US West Coast.
